correctness.rationale: For the corrected statement, the four-layer argument holds (the antipode reaches a sink in at most three steps and any layer-two vertex can use it in at most one extra step), and the listed witness forces four. Independently exhausted 4096 orientations using forward reach-set growth to depth seven; recovered 962 with no sink, 3134 with a sink, radius counts 258, 644, 1512, 720 and 2492 passing the all-sink test. Recomputed the denominator by inclusion–exclusion and checked the conditional ratios. The frozen text incorrectly equated independent continuous payoffs with fair orientations: independent disjoint action-dependent payoff supports can orient all edges upward almost surely. The repair requires iid atomless entries or fair independent comparisons for the probabilistic interpretation and preserves the deterministic theorem and counts.
residual_risks: No conclusion about arbitrary activation schedules, larger cubes, or nonuniform orientation probabilities.

value.rationale: This is a natural finite benchmark for random-game dynamics and refines the known existence theorem: the cutoff is schedule-independent in its existential sense, and the exact distribution measures how much length is needed at the worst starting state under best choice of updates. Unique-sink games already separate lengths three and four, showing why mere reachability counts do not supply it. The witness and census give reference cases for quantitative work on larger cubes.
residual_risks: Exact finite result only; no stochastic hitting-time or asymptotic claims.
